summary: Bedwell Harbour Seaplane Base (YBW) is a small floatplane facility located on Mayne Island in British Columbia's Southern Gulf Islands, serving as a convenient gateway for travelers heading to the island communities between Vancouver and Victoria. The base supports scheduled and charter floatplane operations, connecting the remote Gulf Islands to mainland British Columbia and Vancouver Island. Its sheltered harbour location makes it a practical year-round access point for residents and visitors exploring the Gulf Islands archipelago.
faqs:
Q: Where is Bedwell Harbour Seaplane Base located?
A: It is situated on the west side of Mayne Island in the Southern Gulf Islands of British Columbia, Canada, roughly halfway between Vancouver and Victoria.

Q: What type of aircraft use this base?
A: The facility handles float-equipped (seaplane) aircraft only, as it operates as a water aerodrome rather than a land-based airport.

Q: Are there scheduled flights to YBW?
A: Several regional seaplane carriers offer scheduled or charter service connecting Mayne Island to Vancouver, Victoria, and other Gulf Island communities.

Q: Is the base open year-round?
A: Yes, the seaplane base operates throughout the year, weather and harbour conditions permitting.
transport_tips: Getting to the seaplane base typically involves traveling to one of the mainland or Vancouver Island terminals first, then transferring to a connecting floatplane flight. If arriving from Vancouver, passengers usually depart from a downtown Vancouver seaplane terminal, while those from Victoria typically fly from the Inner Harbour. There is no road access to the seaplane base itself, so onward travel on Mayne Island requires arranging local pickup, taxi, or walking from the dock area.
local_tip: Pack light and bring a soft-sided bag if possible—floatplane luggage compartments are much smaller than commercial airline overhead bins, and soft bags make loading into the float pontoons easier.
